setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned with different velocities for four notes: 127, 117, 107, 97 and 100, 100, 100, 100. Its notes come from a third pattern, shown on the screen as Note mode PAT 4 (pattern 4 is not assigned to the channel; all its notes are MIDI 67), so only velocity changes. Velocity merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each velocity is the mean of the two sources, for example (127 + 100) / 2 = 114, so the four notes sound at 114, 109, 104 and 99. Read the velocities in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": every note is MIDI 67 and only the velocity changes.
steps.title: Average velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once, without K1 (with K1 held the same button sets length merge instead). The button lights brighter and Velocity mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the sources.
steps.title: Choose Higher

steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 127, 126, 111 and 102. The first is 114 + 27 = 141, limited to 127. Use Higher to accent a step.
steps.title: Higher velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) again. The button changes again and Velocity mode reads DOWN, the manual's Lower: twice the lowest source minus the mean.
steps.title: Choose Lower

steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 86, 91, 96 and 95. The first is 2 x 100 - 114 = 86. Use Lower for ghost notes.
steps.title: Lower velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once more. The modes cycle Average, Higher, Lower and back: tap Play and the MIDI strip shows the velocities 114, 109, 104 and 99 again.
steps.title: Return to Average
